Truckers in Nuevo Laredo are standing down, at least for now, after Mexico's Interior Ministry (Segob) and national trucking organizations agreed Tuesday, Oct. 27, to end highway blockades and suspend protests in exchange for work tables to address the sector's demands, according to El Mañana de Nuevo Laredo.

The agreement, reached after a meeting with the Cámara Nacional del Autotransporte de Carga (Canacar), commits participating organizations to definitively remove blockades and suspend freight protests, Segob said. Four work tables were set up to take up highway security, infrastructure, tax issues, social security and labor conditions, with Segob's undersecretariat and Government Unit coordinating follow-up, according to national reports of the ministry's statement.

For Nuevo Laredo, the pause follows two days of local mobilization. Truckers joined a national mobilization Monday, Oct. 26, and on Tuesday about 50 trailers protested on the highway — stopping on the road, not on the international bridge — according to earlier local coverage. Leaders told drivers to disperse and return to their places of origin, leaving highways clear, according to national trucking leaders quoted in the coverage.

The suspension is temporary in the sense that the underlying demands are not yet resolved: the work tables are meant to produce concrete results, and the sector's complaints — including highway insecurity, attacks on drivers, extortion, over-regulation and deteriorating infrastructure — remain on the table, according to the trucking organizations. No new mobilizations were announced as part of the agreement.

For a border city whose economy runs on cross-border freight, the end of the blockades removes an immediate disruption to highway circulation, even as the negotiations that will decide whether the peace holds are just beginning.

title: Nuevo Laredo truckers suspend protests after Segob deal sets up four work tables
